To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LFERs based either on one-electron reduction potential or LUMO energies explain a substantial fraction of the variability in the rates of dechlorination of chlorinated hydrocarbons by zero-valent Fe.

the dehalogenation rate constants of a series of chlorinated hydrocarbons by Fe0 can be predicted from their LUMO energies, and the LUMO energies are related to the reduction potential of the halogenated hydrocarbon.

the correlation between rate constants for reductive dechlorination of chlorinated aliphatic compounds by zero-valent metal is improved by using one-electron reduction potential or lowest unoccupied molecular orbit energy (ELUMO) as the descriptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetics of dechlorination by Fe0, which is a promising technology for the remediation of groundwater contaminated with chlorinated aliphatic compounds.
the development of predictive tools for dechlorination of chlorinated alkenes and alkanes by zero-valant iron.
the kinetics and mechanisms of reductive dechlorination of chlorinated organic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the LFERs presented here provide an excellent tool for predicting dechlorination rates by Fe0 for chloroalkanes and chloroalkenes, and that the correlations based on one-electron reduction potential and LUMO energy provide the best predictions.

LFERs based either on two-electron reduction potential or one-electron reduction potential and estimated LUMO energy provide a reasonable description of the kinetics of dechlorination of chlorinated aliphatic hydrocarbons by Fe0.
there is a linear relationship between the rate constants for dehalogenations of chlorinated hydrocarbons by zero valent iron and the LUMO energy of these compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best LFERs for the kinetics of dechlorination by Fe0 are based on one-electron reduction potential, but that two-electron reduction potential can be used if one is aware that there is a systematic error in the relationship.
LFERs based upon ELUMO are more successful in predicting dechlorination by Fe0 than those based on E1/2.

dechlorination rates are not correlated with two-electron reduction potential (E2), but they are correlated with one-electron reduction potential and LUMO energy, both of which can be estimated with semiempirical quantum chemical methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LFERs can explain and predict the rates of dechlorination by zero-valent metal particles.
LFERs can be developed for reductive dehalogenation reactions, which can be useful for predicting the rates of dehalogena- tion reactions in the environment.
the LUMO energy is a good descriptor of the reactivity of halogenated alkanes and halogenated alkenes in Fe0 dehalogenation.
